_about: Quest templates for 1950 (data only, nothing reads them yet). A quest is a small chain: a NEED (a regular, a place or a happening) + 1 to 3 STEPS using existing verbs + a RESOLUTION. Slots are filled by the world from its seeds; each template must be good enough alone (ALIVE-SEA mini-quest grill 1-2). No quest log, no money, no time limits by default; at most one or two offered at once; ignored quests fade gently with a "fade" line.
_spec: games/windward/docs/ALIVE-SEA.md: "Grill: generated mini quests" (rounds 1 to 3), "the thing model" (rumours, regulars, warmth), "anchoring", "day and night". Ids link to data/things-1950.json (things), artifacts-1950.json, quests-1950.json, rumours-1950.json and data/island-lore.json.
_invented: Everything here is INVENTED unless a record says otherwise: each carries invented:true and a source {kind, refs}. Spoken lines are INVENTED-DIALOGUE, short, for Felix to rewrite by eye. No real private person is named.

_fields.name: short title
_fields.firstSlice: true for the three templates of the first quest slice (ALIVE-SEA mini quests, round 3, item 17)
_fields.giver: a people thing id, or a {slot}; null when the quest starts from a happening (see trigger)
_fields.trigger: { thing, note }: the quest is offered when the player meets this thing
_fields.slots: { name: { type, from?, rule?, label?, spawn?, spot?, nameable? } }: what the world fills in. type is one of _vocab.slotTypes
_fields.steps: 1 to 3 of { verb, what?, where?, to?, using?, when?, returns?, note? }; verb is one of _vocab.verbs; ids or {slots} in what/where/to
_fields.resolution: { text, receiver }: what happens at the end
_fields.reward: { warmth: small | medium, gift?: { artifacts: [ids] } | { tier, pool: [ids], teller?: slot }, rumour?: { from: thing id or slot }, knowledge?: text, nameGift?: true }. A gift is never a unique (those are only placed by Felix).
_fields.offeredWhen: { timeOfDay?, weather?, season?, storyPhase? } (same vocabulary as things-1950.json)
_fields.softDeadline: optional: a time that matters ("before the ferry"), not a limit; missing it triggers the fade line
_fields.lines: { offer, done: { gruff, chatty, shy }, fade }: short, in the giver's voice; {slots} are filled in
_fields.seeds: the island-lore.json quest seeds this template grows from: { place, hook: questSeeds, index }
_fields.loreTeller: the regular who tells the true story of a rare gift (ALIVE-SEA 13)

_vocab.verbNotes: sail to, find, pick up, carry, deliver, be there at a time/weather are the settled existing verbs; hail, tell and name come from the tap, quest and names grills.

skerry.rule: a skerry within sight of the giver, on the lee side of where the last blow came from

storm.rule: a label for the last blow, given by the weather system (last night's blow, the gale on Tuesday)

resolution.text: The giver is glad to have it back. Word gets round the quay that you are good with small things.

offer.gruff: {storm} took my {item}. Find it and I'll not forget.
offer.chatty: You'll never guess! {storm} took my {item}. Out by the skerries, I'd say. Would you look?
offer.shy: Excuse me... {storm} took my {item}. Could you look for it?

done.chatty: My {item}! You found it! Here, take this, I insist!
done.shy: Oh. Thank you. I had given it up.

lines.fade: Never mind. It washed up by itself in the end.

source.note: Generic template. Lore variants: Gullholmen (a fish box for a tin of mackerel), Måseskär (a winch handle: also its own template), Käringön (a net float). The need and lines are INVENTED.

resolution.text: The receiver is glad of it and talks for a minute: that is how you hear things.

offer.chatty: Would you take {object} across to {receiver}? You'd be doing me a real kindness!
offer.shy: Um... could you take {object} to {receiver}? If it's on your way.

done.gruff: Good. Right on time. Sit down a minute.
done.chatty: Oh, wonderful! {object}, just what I wanted. Have you heard the news?
done.shy: Thank you. Please, stay a moment.

lines.fade: Never mind. It went with the ferry in the end.

source.note: Generic template; the lore variants are each a sourced errand pattern. A tin of paint is the folded-in version of the Jämningarna "repaint the belt" seed (repainting is not an existing verb).

trigger.note: offered when you find a drifting boat after a blow

resolution.text: The owner is relieved. The keeper reads the drift for you and tells the true story of an old thing from the sea, which he gives you.

offer.gruff: That's my boat. Where did you find her?
offer.chatty: My boat! My boat! I thought she was gone for good! Where was she?
offer.shy: That... that is my boat. Where was she?

done.gruff: Good lad. Go and ask the keeper where she came from.
done.chatty: You have no idea what this means! The keeper knows the currents. Go on, ask him!
done.shy: Thank you. The keeper may know where she drifted from.

lines.fade: Never mind. She came home on the next tide.

source.note: Generic template. For this template the offer lines are the OWNER's first words, because the quest starts when you find the boat. The keeper is story-owned: his scene is Felix's, the lore he tells is the artifact's true story. The rare gifts are three wreck relics; none is a unique candidate.

spawn.rule: in the shallows at the landing, visible when the boat is slow

resolution.text: He is so relieved he talks about the mainland for ten minutes.

offer.gruff: Dropped the winch handle in the harbour. Find it.
offer.chatty: I've done something stupid! The winch handle went over the side at the landing. Could you fish it out? Please?
offer.shy: The winch handle... I dropped it. At the landing. Could you...?

done.chatty: You found it! I could kiss you. Have a mantle, we have loads. Now tell me about Lysekil!

lines.fade: Never mind. The keeper made a new one from a boathook.

source.note: the need, the steps and the lines are INVENTED; the lore quest seed is itself an invented hook

templates.name: A float for the quarry sound

resolution.text: The quarryman turns it over in his hands; it is his father's.

offer.gruff: This float is not mine. Take it to Tornö.
offer.chatty: See this float? It's a Tornö float, it came back with the storm. Could you take it over?
offer.shy: This float... it belongs on Tornö. Would you take it?

done.chatty: It is! It's my father's! Sit down, sit down, let me tell you about the Dora!
done.shy: Thank you. It means a lot.

lines.fade: Never mind. Somebody else took it over.

from: a parcel of newspapers and a letter

resolution.text: She is cross that it is late and glad that it came.

offer.gruff: Parcel for Gåsö. Boarding house. Go.
offer.chatty: There's a parcel for the boarding house on Gåsö, papers and a letter. Would you take it? She hates to wait!
offer.shy: Is it too much to ask? A parcel for Gåsö. For the boarding house.

done.chatty: At last! Two weeks of papers at once. Come in, come in, I have news!
done.shy: Oh. Thank you. I was getting worried.

lines.fade: Never mind. It went with the post boat.

templates.name: A name for the seal skerry

skerry.rule: an unnamed skerry within 300 m of the seal rocks west of Storön

when.still: about a minute, so the seals come back

resolution.text: The boy writes the name in his notebook. From now on it is on your chart with the name you gave it.

offer.gruff: That skerry has no name. Give it one.
offer.chatty: You know, that skerry has no name at all. And the seals sleep on it! Will you name it with me?
offer.shy: It has no name. The seals sleep there. Could you... name it?

done.chatty: That's the best name! I'm writing it down. Now it is real!

lines.fade: Never mind. We just called it the seal rock.

source.note: The names grill (ALIVE-SEA 19): only skerries with no real name; era-fitting suggestions plus free text; the name lives in the host's world.

from: a wrapped parcel of buns from the bakery

resolution.text: The teacher unwraps the buns on the pier and shares one.

softDeadline.note: before the teacher's Saturday boat leaves for Lysekil; after that she has gone

offer.gruff: Bakery parcel. Stora Kornö. The teacher. Morning.
offer.chatty: There's a parcel from the bakery for the teacher on Kornö! Before the Saturday boat, or she'll be gone!
offer.shy: A parcel for the teacher on Kornö. If you could. Before she leaves.

done.chatty: Buns! Still warm! You are a saint. Look what I found on the beach.

lines.fade: Never mind. She had her buns in Lysekil in the end.

source.note: the need, the steps and the lines are INVENTED; the lore seed (Stora Kornö, questSeeds[0]) says the Lysekil bakery, but the giver now stands at Fiskebäckskil, so the parcel is simply from "the bakery"

resolution.text: A swap that suited everyone, and the deckhand has a bit of gossip to go with the flour.

offer.gruff: Mackerel to the Lysekil stall. Flour back. Simple.
offer.chatty: Take this basket of mackerel over to the Lysekil market stall and bring back flour! You'll see: it's a good swap!
offer.shy: Could you take mackerel to the stall in Lysekil? And bring back flour? If it's not too much.

done.chatty: Flour! Perfect! You can have the first bun, I mean it!
done.shy: Thank you. It saves me the crossing.

lines.fade: Never mind. I went over myself in the end.

offer.chatty: This is the part the Grundsund skipper has been howling about! Fixed at last. Take it over!

done.shy: Thank you. I'll start at once.

from: a painted buoy on a short line

steps.note: drop it at the marked spot over the wreck

resolution.text: Now his lines miss the wreck and the wreck ground is on your chart.

reward.knowledge: the Freya wreck ground is marked on your chart

offer.gruff: Buoy the Freya. My lines keep snagging.
offer.chatty: Every hook I own is on that wreck! If you buoy her, I'll keep clear. Would you?
offer.shy: The Freya... she catches my lines. Could you mark her?

done.chatty: Finally! No more snagging! You are a lifesaver! Come and see something later.

lines.fade: Never mind. I've moved my lines.

source.note: Warmth medium unlocks secret.harpo.ships-bell (requires warm). The verb "deliver at a spot" stands in for dropping a buoy.
